note: wire_cases are verified as a runtime verifier does before any receiver state: `reject_reason` names the first refusal in the contract's verification order. Accepted wire cases that a runtime must still refuse for its own state are exercised in runtime_sequences. mapping_cases give the disposition each trigger emits, or null. In runtime_sequences, `seal` records an artifact the runtime sealed for delivery; `disposition` presents a wire case; `ack` is `applied` or `refused:<reason>`; `reoffers` and `checkpoints` say whether the runtime would re-offer the current epoch's registration and issue periodic checkpoints, and `envelopes` whether it hands off new envelopes; `delivery_state` is `handed_off` or `stopped` for an artifact just sealed; `queued_ack` records a verified gateway custody acknowledgement; `local_stopped` counts sealed, unacknowledged artifacts held locally in a stopped scope and `gateway_custodied` those acknowledged; `reoffers_epoch` asks the same per epoch; and the health fields are those of runtime-health/v2. `at_ms` on a `seal` or `disposition` step is the runtime's clock when it sealed the artifact or recorded the stop, and `bytes` the artifact's encoded size; `configuration_change` changes the runtime configuration; `identity_replacement` starts the named replacement identity under the named epoch; `retired_identity_stopped` lists retired identities whose identity stop record is kept; `stopped_local_artifact_count`, `stopped_local_bytes` and `oldest_stopped_local_since_ms` are the runtime-health/v2 fields, across every epoch of the current identity; `retired_stopped_local` gives, per retired identity, the count and bytes of its stopped-local artifacts, kept and queryable under that identity only. `handoff_deferred` on a `seal` marks an artifact whose handoff had not begun, and `handoff_unrecorded` one handed off with no durable record of when its handoff began, which the runtime therefore cannot prove preceded a stop. `reoffer_schedule` fixes the registration re-offer schedule: `delays_s` are the delays before re-offers 1, 2, 3 and so on; a due case asks whether re-offer `attempt` is due `since_previous_offer_s` seconds after the previous offer; a restart case asks the same at `now_s` for a runtime restarted at `restart_s` after an offer at `previous_offer_s`; and an overdue case asks whether an obligation pending since `pending_since_s`, across restarts at `restarts_at_s`, is overdue at `now_s`, all in runtime seconds.

runtime_sequences.name: retained_pending suspends re-offers and a later confirmation completes them
a terminal disposition closes the registration attempt and a fresh reference repairs it
an artifact-scoped disposition on a checkpoint does not stop later checkpoints
an epoch-scoped disposition stops offers only for that epoch
an identity-scoped disposition stops offers and checkpoints and survives restart
an invalid, wrong-purpose, stale or wrong-device disposition changes nothing
a disposition never changes Tier C or Tier D execution, and local recording continues
a replacement identity starts an independent lifecycle
a confirmation for an epoch this device never registered changes nothing
an epoch change leaves the previous epoch's obligation re-offered until it resolves
an identity stop keeps sealing locally, hands off nothing new, and keeps custody where it is
an epoch stop leaves another epoch's handoff running
delivery_stop_status asserts nothing about connectivity: a disconnected gateway leaves it not_stopped
stopped-local counts are zero and null before any stop, and a current-epoch stop counts, keeps and only lawfully releases its local artifacts
a historical stopped epoch stays stopped and counted through configuration, a new commissioning reference, a new epoch and restart
an identity stop is lifted by no later disposition and survives identity replacement, its records kept under the retired identity and not counted for the replacement
an acknowledgement for bytes whose handoff had not begun before the stop is inconsistent state, as is one the runtime cannot prove or one for bytes it never sealed
a new stop on the replacement identity counts only the replacement identity's artifacts, and the retired identity's stay queryable under it
